slot.brief: Sentence with a tense inconsistency across clauses (e.g., past event described with present perfect later); identify the incorrect part.

stem:
In the sentence below, identify the part that contains an error.

**(A)** The committee announced the results **(B)** on Monday, and **(C)** the winning candidate has thanked the volunteers **(D)** that evening.
options: the winning candidate has thanked the volunteers

verdicts.working: “Has thanked” is present perfect, which is incompatible with the definite past-time expression “that evening.” It should be “thanked,” so the error is in (C).

working:
“That evening” refers to a completed time in the past, so use simple past: “thanked.” The other parts are grammatically correct.

Independent check: “Has thanked” is present perfect, which is incompatible with the definite past-time expression “that evening.” It should be “thanked,” so the error is in (C).
solution: “That evening” refers to a definite, completed time in the past, so the simple past is required: “the winning candidate thanked the volunteers that evening.”
